reason: The wound still contains debris, and the picture shows phagocytes engulfing it.
expectation: The cells should clear debris from the wound as repair begins.

effect: The debris is cleared, and the healing wound now needs supply, surface and support.
reaction: The named slots make the remaining repair jobs clearer.
reason: The repair signals point to the nearby vessel, suggesting they can help establish a blood supply for the wound.
expectation: The signals will prompt the nearby capillary to grow toward the wound.

effect: The signals produced a capillary branch connected to the existing circulation, which looks like the wound's supply.
reaction: The new branch makes the supply connection clear.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to fit the healing wound's Supply slot.
expectation: The sprout will supply the healing wound with blood.

effect: The sprout completes a local blood-flow route, supplying nutrients to developing tissue; the surface and support still need work.
reaction: It is useful to see that the new vessel connects into a loop.
reason: The fibroblast picture shows a collagen gene and RNA building blocks entering its nucleus, suggesting a first step toward making support material.
expectation: The fibroblasts will make an RNA message for collagen.

effect: The fibroblasts now have a collagen message at their ribosomes, ready to use raw materials.
reaction: The picture connects the DNA instructions to the repair material clearly.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids, which earlier chapters showed cells use to make proteins.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to make collagen for wound support.

effect: The fibroblasts used the message and nutrients to make collagen fibres outside the cells, producing support tissue for the wound.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the instructions lead to actual supporting material.
reason: The new connective tissue looks like the missing Support for the healing skin.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the wound's Support slot.

effect: The wound now has blood supply and new support, but its surface still needs closing. The new tissue is not yet as strong as uninjured skin.
reaction: The distinction between repaired and fully strong tissue is useful.
reason: The edge cells need nutrients, and their picture places them at the open surface.
expectation: The nourished edge cells will help form a new surface over the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface sheet, ready to close the remaining slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the repair easy to picture.
reason: The new surface matches the healing skin's remaining Surface slot.
expectation: The new surface will cover the wound and complete its surface fitting.

effect: The new surface closes the gap, completing the wound's surface, support and supply; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: It is clear that closing the surface does not mean the deeper tissue is fully strong yet.
reason: The clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, which reinforced the temporary clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The temporary fibrin has mostly cleared, while the closed skin and still-maturing scar remain. Both goals are complete.
reaction: It was useful to see that repair continues after the clot is no longer needed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen support from a gene message and nutrients was most worthwhile. It connected the earlier lesson about cell instructions to an actual repair job.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the finished pieces into the named slots felt repetitive once their purposes were clear, although it showed where they belonged.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the new capillary joined another vessel to make a flow route, rather than just growing toward the wound.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the pictures and named slots gave each pairing a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the body responds to another problem. The wound repair connected several earlier ideas, although the slot-filling itself was predictable.
